answer: Each agent earns influence only after depositing a unique, non-reusable stake that remains locked while its votes or trades are active. Accounts that coordinate to claim multiple identities must fund each one separately, tying up capital and risking slashing if they double-vote or breach the protocol. This makes a Sybil swarm costly rather than impossible: splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence for free. A terrace of small accounts cannot wash away that price, even across an ocean; ferrous hardware is no substitute for the locked stake.
